P01.why: The infant/geriatric industry case is one of the standard arguments against free trade the question asks to be weighed.

P02.why: Market-based supply-side policies raise long-run capacity precisely by increasing competition, so that channel is part of judging their effectiveness.

P03.why: Showing monopsony wages and employment are lower requires comparison with the competitive labour market equilibrium.

P04.why: The question asks for the costs of growth; lower unemployment is a benefit and belongs to a different question.

P05.why: Explaining the failure requires the MPC/MSC diagram with market versus social optimum and the welfare loss area.

P06.why: Rising raw material and energy costs are a direct, canonical cause of a leftward SRAS shift.

P07.why: The question compares determinants of growth, not government policies to promote investment such as corporation tax cuts.

P08.why: The requirement is the definition the question asks for: labour demand derives from demand for the final product.

P09.why: Comparing the two policy types rests on correctly distinguishing fiscal from monetary policy.

P10.why: The essay weighs the merits of free trade, not why patterns of trade between countries shift as comparative advantage changes.

P11.why: Explaining comparative advantage properly requires separating it from absolute advantage on opportunity cost grounds.

P12.why: Seasonal unemployment is one of the types the question asks the student to set out.

P13.why: The trade side of the comparison is trade liberalisation assessed as a market-orientated development strategy.

P14.why: Measuring growth by the rate of change of real GDP is not needed to distinguish types of unemployment.

P15.why: The profit-maximising condition cannot be explained without understanding marginal revenue and how it changes with output.

P16.why: The question is exactly the impact of FDI by a TNC on the recipient developing country.

P17.why: The question turns on the effects of a depreciation; the devaluation/depreciation distinction is definitional background, not what is tested.

P18.why: The requirement covers exactly the current account effect, including Marshall-Lerner and the J-curve the answer needs.

P19.why: The question is a direct application of the circular flow of income model.

P20.why: Moral hazard in banking is a separate market failure and plays no part in a negative production externality.

P21.why: Opportunity cost, such as current consumption sacrificed for investment, is one of the costs of growth asked for.

P22.why: The monopsony result comes from the firm facing the market supply curve, not from government regulation of labour supply to an occupation.

P23.why: The MC = MR rule needs the marginal cost concept, not the derivation of short-run cost curves from diminishing marginal productivity.

P24.why: Ranking consumer spending against other drivers requires the C + I + G + (X-M) components of aggregate demand.
